question: Does libRoadRunner, behind the stand-in's interface, reproduce Schoeberl2002 and the models the stand-in already ran, against BioModels' curation figures, at a tolerance fixed before the runs?

BIOMD0000000019.name: Schoeberl2002 - EGF MAPK
BIOMD0000000019.figure: BioModels BIOMD0000000019 curation_image.png: 'time course of active species as in fig. 2 c,d,e,f'; integration by SBMLODESolver (20080507); 4 panels, 0-60 min; red 50, blue 0.5, green 0.125 ng/ml EGF

BIOMD0000000010.name: Kholodenko2000 - MAPK oscillations
BIOMD0000000010.figure: BioModels BIOMD0000000010 curation_image.png: Figure 2A reproduced with Copasi 4.10 (Build 55); MAPK (green) and MAPK-PP (blue), nM, 0-150 min; x calibrated on the tick labels, 3.653 px/min

BIOMD0000000012.name: Elowitz2000 - Repressilator
BIOMD0000000012.figure: BioModels BIOMD0000000012 curation_image.png: protein numbers as in figure 1c, deterministic run with SBML ODESolver; the notes say it departs from the paper before 400 min (initial conditions), so only 400-1000 min is read; red LacI (PX), orange TetR (PY), blue cI (PZ)

BIOMD0000000084.name: Hornberg2005 - ERK cascade
BIOMD0000000084.figure: BioModels BIOMD0000000084 curation_image.jpeg: the plot of Fig 2, simulated with MathSBML; top R over 0-2, bottom x1p (green), x2p (blue), x3p (red) over 0-50; axes calibrated on the tick labels (top 139.5 px per unit time, 362.5 px per unit level; bottom 5.8 and 320)

BIOMD0000000116.name: McClean2007 - CrossTalk
BIOMD0000000116.figure: BioModels BIOMD0000000116 curation_image.png is a parameter scan (Supplementary Figure 2, COPASI 4.0.20), not a time course: no feature is read, the engines are compared only

money: none: public BioModels files, no key

sources.version: the SBML main files as downloaded, sha256 per input; references read from the entries' curation_image files (genomeos/molecules/sbml_reference.py)

result_manifest.assembly: n/a: kinetic models, no genome coordinates
result_manifest.coordinates: n/a: kinetic models, no genome coordinates

exclusions.reason: McClean2007: its curation figure is a parameter scan, not a time course; compared on both engines, not scored

result_manifest.partitions: n/a: nothing was fitted; the references are read from figures, not trained on

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record b933129

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
